newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major attacks Labour's job creation scheme.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major attacks Labour's job creation scheme.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Thursday attacked Labour's welfare-to-work programme, saying it would replace real jobs with short-term phoney ones.
Labour plans to offer employers 60 pounds a week to take on an unemployed young person.
Speaking at a news conference, Major challenged Labour leader Tony Blair to explain how he would stop employers getting rid of other young people who did not attract the 60 pounds subsidy.
"Labour's plans mean a massive transfer of jobs from the private sector to the public sector. They would replace real jobs for young people with short-term phoney ones," Major said.
Furthermore, Labour's pledge to introduce a minimum wage and to sign the European Union's social chapter on workers' rights would throw more young people out of work.
"The truth is: Labour would need to have an employment scheme funded by the taxpayer merely to scoop up the young people thrown out of work by their other policies," Major said.
